🚨Newly released 911 audio and surveillance footage expose the terrifying final moments of 68 year old Frank Imhoff, who was killed while simply loading his trailer at a Port Neches, Texas, storage facility.

​According to investigators, the Nederland resident was working outside his pickup truck when a suspect identified as Dekovin Flanagan Jr. suddenly leaped across the hood of the vehicle and stole it. As the truck sped off, Imhoff was run over, suffering fatal injuries.

​Flanagan was later tracked down and apprehended by law enforcement at a nearby apartment complex. He is currently being held on a $1 million bond facing murder charges.

​Investigators are still piecing together a motive, noting that it remains entirely unclear why Imhoff's truck was targeted or what triggered the violent escalation.
​
Case Backstory & Investigation Details

The fatal incident occurred on August 16, 2026, at Central Maxi Storage located on Ridgewood Drive in Port Neches, Texas.

​The Victim: 68 year old Frank Cameron Imhoff of Nederland, Texas, was a dedicated father and grandfather affectionately known as "Campa" to his grandchildren.

Family members noted that he was hardworking and would naturally try to protect his livelihood. 

According to the Port Neches Police Department and investigative affidavits, the suspect identified as Dekovin Keith Flanagan Jr. (21, of Port Arthur, Texas) had initially wandered into and rummaged through an unoccupied storage unit on the property. 

Flanagan then sprinted out, hopped the hood of Imhoff’s pickup truck while it was being loaded with a trailer, forced his way into the driver's seat, and attempted to speed away.

As Flanagan accelerated in the stolen vehicle, surveillance footage captured Imhoff running alongside the driver's side trying to stop the theft before being knocked down and run over by his own truck and trailer.

Following a chaotic morning that involved erratic behavior and property destruction at a nearby apartment complex, law enforcement tracked Flanagan down to the Ridgewood Apartments, where officers found him hiding in a closet.

Dekovin Keith Flanagan Jr.’s specific upcoming trial date or docket appearance has not yet been publicly scheduled or published in local court records.

posts.text:
Over the past week, I’ve been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I've never met. Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me.

I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. NVIDIA has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like NVIDIA be possible. I love our country, and I love NVIDIA.

I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation. 

Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.

Thank you again to everyone who has shared their good wishes. I am profoundly humbled by your support. To my family: I love you, and I will spend the rest of my life being worthy of yours.

Jensen

The strike and  resulting destruction of the Kerch Bridge is a turning point. It carries both symbolic and practical significance.

The Kerch Bridge is the main symbol of the Russian occupation of Ukrainian Crimea and the embodiment of illegal annexation for Ukraine. It represents much more than just a transportation artery. For Russia and Putin, it is a symbol of "greatness" and control over Crimea. It is Putin's flagship project. The construction of the bridge was framed by Russian propaganda as the "construction of the century" and a personal achievement of Putin, who personally opened it in 2018 driving a KAMAZ truck.

For the Kremlin, the bridge became material proof that Crimea is "forever" connected to the territory of the Russian Federation and fully integrated into Russia. For years, Russian authorities called the crossing "the most protected object in the world." Thus, each successful strike on the bridge further shatters the myth of the invincibility of Russian air defense and Ukraine's inability to reach key targets in Russia's deep rear.

For us, Ukrainians, the Kerch Bridge is a symbol of occupation and the inevitability of de-occupation. The bridge is a symbol of the violation of international law and sovereignty. The crossing was used primarily for the transfer of Russian troops, equipment, and weapons, turning Crimea into a massive military base and a springboard for an offensive on the south of Ukraine. A successful strike on the bridge is a turning point. It is a demonstration that Ukraine can and will defeat the enemy. It is a demonstration that the Kremlin's positions are vulnerable even in those regions that Moscow considered its untouchable rear.

Crimea has de facto found itself in a blockade. There are no ferries or railways, and the only navigable channel is blocked.

The occupied peninsula is becoming critically dependent on the "Novorossiya" highway through the Russian-occupied territories of the Zaporizhzhia and Kherson regions, which Russians have been calling the "road of death" for some time now. Ukraine's Defense Forces have established dense remote fire control over the highway, turning the 700-kilometer overland corridor into a vulnerable zone.

A strike on the Kerch Bridge will directly affect the Russian "Dniepr" troop grouping and the logistics connectivity factor. The "Dniepr" grouping operates in the Kherson and Zaporizhzhia directions and received a significant portion of its ammunition, fuel, and heavy equipment through Crimean hubs. The loss of full-fledged railway and road communication across the Kerch Strait will force Russians to stretch their supply lines from the Rostov region, making convoys even more vulnerable to strike weapons.

Of course, the Russian propaganda machine will employ information isolation of the region and will shift its audience's focus to other topics to avoid panic and criticism of the central authorities. A similar scenario was observed during the Ukrainian operation in Russia's Kursk region.

For Ukraine, this creates a window of opportunity for targeted information work via local Telegram channels and word of mouth, highlighting the inability of Moscow and Putin to guarantee security and basic provisions to the residents of the peninsula.
